meanings.usage: 指看似真实但实际不存在的事物或想法
形容乡村或田园生活方式
常用复数形式raptures表示极度欣喜

meanings.meaning: adj/verb. 闪烁的，闪闪发光的
meanings.usage: 形容光线反射的闪烁效果

meanings.meaning: 田园诗般的，完美无缺的
meanings.usage: 形容平静美好的乡村生活
表示对某事持怀疑态度
指认识但不太熟的人，区别于friend
形容坚持己见不肯改变的态度
形容因负重或疲劳而走路不稳
指某种状态或氛围突然到来

meanings.meaning: exotic；adj. 导乎寻常的，外来的

phrases.usage: 表示极度兴奋或欣喜若狂

examples.en: They always go into raptures at the mere mention of the country.
examples.zh: 他们一提到乡村就会欣喜若狂。

phrases.usage: 表示无法理解或超出能力范围

examples.en: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day is beyond me.
examples.zh: 我无法理解为什么人们愿意每天忍受四个小时的旅程。

phrases.usage: 表示没有某物也能应付，没有也行

examples.en: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best.
examples.zh: 如果你能不要乡村的那点乐趣，你会发现城市能给你最好的生活。

examples.en: There is so much variety that you never have to make do with second best.
examples.zh: 品种繁多，你永远不必凑合用次品。

phrases.usage: 表示疯狂、放纵、胡乱购物

examples.en: Country people run wild when they go shopping in the city.
examples.zh: 乡下人进城购物时会疯狂采购。

phrases.usage: 表示接近尾声，即将结束

examples.en: As the play draws to its close, they wonder whether they will ever catch that last train home.
examples.zh: 当戏剧接近尾声时，他们担心能否赶得上最后一班回家的火车。

phrases.usage: 表示被藏起来，安置在某个地方

examples.en: The thousands that travel to work every day are tucked away in their homes in the country.
examples.zh: 每天成千上万进城工作的人都被藏在乡村的家中。

phrases.phrase: It has always been a mystery to me
phrases.usage: 表示对某人来说一直是个谜

examples.en: It has always been a mystery to me why city dwellers pretend they would prefer to live in the country.
examples.zh: 我一直不明白为什么城里人偏要假装喜欢住在乡下。

phrases.usage: 表示误以为，持有错误的观念

examples.en: Even he still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.
examples.zh: 甚至他仍然误以为乡村生活比城市生活优越。

phrases.usage: 表示为了某种不值得的特权/好处

examples.en: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day for the dubious privilege of living in the country.
examples.zh: 为什么人们愿意每天忍受四小时的路程，就为了住乡下的那个并不值得的好处。

grammar.title: 宾语从句（Object Clause）
grammar.structure: 连接词（that/whether/why/what等）+ 主语 + 谓语 + 其他成分
grammar.definition: 由连接词引导的充当句子宾语的从句，说明说话人对某事物的看法或疑问。 用于表达观点、看法、疑问等内容，可位于动词或介词之后。常见动词如：think, believe, know, wonder, understand等后常接宾语从句。

examples.en: He still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.
examples.zh: 他仍然误以为乡村生活比城市生活优越。

examples.en: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day is beyond me.
examples.zh: 我不明白为什么人们愿意每天忍受四小时的路程。

examples.en: It has always been a mystery to me why city dwellers pretend they would prefer to live in the country.
examples.zh: 我一直不明白为什么城里人偏要假装喜欢住在乡下。

grammar.title: 否定副词置于句首的倒装句
grammar.structure: 否定词/半否定词 + 助动词/be动词/情态动词 + 主语 + 动词原形 + 其他
grammar.definition: 含有never, seldom, rarely, little, nowhere, hardly等否定词或半否定词时，如置于句首，句子需要部分倒装。 强调否定意义，使句子更加正式或文学化。阅读时需注意识别这种倒装结构。

examples.en: Never have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
examples.zh: 我从未见过如此美丽的日落。

examples.en: Seldom does he go to the theatre.
Rarely can you find a place so quiet.
examples.zh: 你很少能找到如此安静的地方。

grammar.title: 条件状语从句（真实条件句）
grammar.structure: If + 主语 + 一般现在时, 主语 + will/can/may + 动词原形
grammar.definition: 表示在某种条件下可能会发生的情况，使用if引导，描述可能实现的假设。 用于提出真实的假设条件，说明条件与结果之间的关系。这类句子被称为第一类条件句，表示可能发生的情况。

examples.en: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best.
examples.zh: 如果你能不要乡村的那点乐趣，你会发现城市能给你最好的生活。

examples.en: If you work hard, you will succeed.
examples.zh: 如果你努力工作，你就会成功。

original.en: Nothing can be compared, he maintains, with the first cockcrow, the twittering of birds at dawn...
original.zh: 他坚持认为，没有什么能比得上清晨的第一声鸡鸣、鸟儿的啾啾叫声...

imitations.en: Nothing can be compared with a mother's love.
imitations.zh: 没有什么能比得上母爱。

imitations.en: Nothing can be compared with the taste of fresh fruit.
imitations.zh: 没有什么能比得上新鲜水果的味道。

original.en: Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day for the dubious privilege of living in the country is beyond me.
original.zh: 我无法理解为什么人们为了在乡村居住这个可疑的特权而愿意每天忍受四小时的旅程。

imitations.en: Why she married him is beyond me.
imitations.zh: 我无法理解她为什么要嫁给他。

imitations.en: Why anyone would want to live there is beyond me.
imitations.zh: 我无法理解为什么有人想住在那里。

original.en: There is something comforting about the warm glow shed by advertisements on cold wet winter nights.
original.zh: 在寒冷潮湿的冬夜，广告牌发出的温暖光芒有一种令人安慰的感觉。

imitations.en: There is something mysterious about the old house.
imitations.zh: 那座老房子有一种神秘的感觉。

imitations.en: There is something fascinating about her stories.
imitations.zh: 她的故事有一种迷人的魅力。

patterns.pattern: If you can do without..., you will find...

original.en: If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best that life can offer.
original.zh: 如果你能放弃乡村的那点乐趣，你就会发现城市能给你提供生活中最好的东西。

imitations.en: If you can do without luxury, you will find life much simpler.
imitations.zh: 如果你能不要奢侈品，你会发现生活简单得多。

imitations.en: If you can do without constant entertainment, you will find time for what matters.
imitations.zh: 如果你能不要不断的娱乐，你会发现时间去做重要的事。

translation:
宁静的乡村生活从来没有吸引过我。我生在城市，长在城市，总认为乡村是透过火车车窗看到的那个样了，或偶尔周末去游玩一下景象。我的许多朋友都住在城市，但他们只要一提起乡村，马上就会变得欣喜若狂。尽管他们都交口称赞宁静的乡村生活的种种优点，但其中只有一个人真去农村住过，而且不足6个月就回来了。即使他也仍存有幻觉，好像乡村生活就是比城市生活优越。他滔滔不绝地大谈友好的农民，洁净的空气，贴近大自然的环境和悠闲的生活节奏。他坚持认为，凌晨雄鸡第一声啼叫，黎明时分小鸟吱喳欢叫，冉冉升起的朝阳染红树木、牧场，此番美景无与伦比。但这种田园诗般的乡村风光仅仅是一个侧面。我的朋友没有提到在电视机前度过的漫长寂寞的冬夜——电视是唯一的娱乐形式。他也不说商店货物品种单调，以及那些每天不得不从乡下赶到城里工作的不幸的人们。人们为什么情愿每天在路上奔波4个小时去换取值得怀疑的乡间的优点，我是无法理解的。要是他们愿意住在本来属于他们的城市，则可以让他们省去诸多不便与节约大量开支。
如果你愿舍弃乡下生活那一点点乐趣的话，那么你会发出城市可以为你提供生活最美好的东西。你去看朋友根本不用跋涉好几英里，因为他们都住在附近，你随时可以同他们聊天或在晚上一起娱乐。我在乡村有一些熟人，他们每年进城来看一回或几回戏，并把此看作一种特殊的享受。看戏在他们是件大事，需要精心计划。当戏快演完时，他们又为是否能赶上末班火车回家而犯愁。这种焦虑，城里人是从未体验过的。坐公共汽车几站路，就可看到最新的展览、电影、戏剧。买东西也是一种乐趣。物品种繁多，从来不必用二等品来凑合。乡里人进城采购欣喜若狂，每次回家时都买足了外来商品，直到拿不动方才罢休，连走路都摇摇晃晃的。城市也并非没有良辰美景。寒冷潮湿的冬夜里，广告灯箱发出的暖光，会给人某种安慰。周末，当成千上万进城上班的人回到他们的乡间寓所之后，空旷的街市笼罩着一种宁静气氛，没有什么能比此时的宁静更令人难忘了。城里人对这一切心里很明白，却偏要执拗地装出他们喜欢住在乡村的样子，这对我来说一直是个谜。

text.title: Illusions of Pastoral peace  宁静田园生活的遐想

lines.en: The quiet life of the country has never appealed to me.
City born and city bred.
I have always regarded the country as something you look at through a train window, or something you occasional visit during the weekend.
Most of my friends live in the city, yet they always go into raptures at the mere mention of the country.
Though they extol the virtues of the peaceful life, only one of them has ever gone to live in the country and he was back in town within six months.
Even he still lives under the illusion that country life is somehow superior to town life.
He is forever talking about the friendly people, the clean atmosphere, the closeness to nature and the gentle pace of living.
Nothing can be compared, he maintains, with the first cockcrow, the twittering of birds at dawn, the sight of the rising sun glinting on the trees and pastures.
This idyllic pastoral scene is only part of the picture.
My friend fails to mention the long and friendless winter evenings in front of the TV -- virtually the only form of entertainment.
He says nothing about the poor selection of goods in the shops, or about those unfortunate people who have to travel from the country to the city every day to get to work.
Why people are prepared to tolerate a four-hour journey each day for the dubious privilege of living in the country is beyond me.
They could be saved so much misery and expense if they chose to live in the city where they rightly belong.
If you can do without the few pastoral pleasures of the country, you will find the city can provide you with the best that life can offer.
You never have to travel miles to see your friends.
They invariably live nearby and are always available for an informal chat or an evening's entertainment.
Some of my acquaintances in the country come up to town once or twice a year to visit the theatre as a special treat.
For them this is a major operation which involves considerable planning.
As the play draws to its close, they wonder whether they will ever catch that last train home.
The cit dweller never experiences anxieties of this sort.
The latest exhibitions, films, or plays are only a short bus ride away.
Shopping, too, is always a pleasure.
The latest exhibitions, films, or plays are only a short bus ride away.
Shopping, too, is always a pleasure.
There is so much variety that you never have to make do with second best.
Country people run wild when they go shopping in the city and stagger home loaded with as many of the exotic items as they can carry.
Nor is the city without its moments of beauty.
There is something comforting about the warm glow shed by advertisements on cold wet winter nights.
Few things could be more impressive than the peace that descends on deserted city streets at weekends when the thousands that travel to work every day are tucked away in their homes in the country.
It has always been a mystery to me who city dwellers , who appreciate all these things, obstinately pretend that they would prefer to live in the country.

lead.summary: 《宁静田园生活的遐想》宁静的乡村生活从来没有吸引过我。我生在城市，长在城市，总认为乡村是透过火车车窗看到的那个样了，或偶尔周末去游玩一下景象。
